licenses.text:
Brenton Septuagint Translation, eBible.org, https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/

The edition's own statement of rights (from eBible.org's copyright page for this
translation):
> "Translation of the Greek Septuagint into English by Sir Lancelot Charles Lee Brenton
Published in 1851, and now in the Public Domain.
If you find errors in the text, please report them so that we can correct them."

Why this is public domain:
Translator: Sir Lancelot Charles Lee Brenton, 2nd Baronet, British. Death year: 1862. First publication: 1851, London, United Kingdom (also named as Samuel Bagster & Sons, London, 1851, in the LXX2012 description on eBible.org). No other person's words are named in this edition.

United States reason: first published in 1851, before 1931, so public domain in the United States in 2026.

Country of origin reason: United Kingdom. Under the Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, section 12(2), copyright ends 70 years after the end of the calendar year of the author's death. Brenton died in 1862, so copyright ended at the end of 1932 and the work is public domain in the United Kingdom.

Sources of these facts:
- https://ebible.org/eng-Brenton/copyright.htm (edition statement, 1851 date)
- https://ebible.org/details.php?id=eng-Brenton (translation details)
- https://ebible.org/eng-uk-lxx2012/ (names the 1851 Samuel Bagster & Sons, London edition)
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancelot_Charles_Lee_Brenton (dates 16 February 1807 to 13 June 1862)
- https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1988/48/section/12 (UK term rule, life plus 70)
- https://www.copyright.gov/title17/92chap3.html (US term rules, 17 U.S.C. chapter 3)

held_out_by.note: eBible's chapter files, <code>_<NNN>_<BOOK>_<CC>_read.txt, are held out by book and chapter, so the same chapter is held out in every translation at once (maintainer's decision, 2026-10-23)

note: eBible.org rebuilds this zip often; the checksum covers the files inside, so a rebuild with the same text still matches.
